summary: Drafted a stable implementation plan for bridging Pi extension UI into Gizmo, outlining how `AgentSession.bindExtensions` would be used with a browser-backed `ExtensionUIContext`, a session-scoped protocol, native dialogs/notifications/widgets, a `@gizmo/extension-ui` web-native component SDK, and a tiered approach to terminal TUI components. The plan was written to `docs/pi-extension-ui-bridge-plan.md` and referenced from `docs/extensions.md`, then formatted with Prettier and committed.
decisions: Do 'Generic Pi UI bridge' first, before redesigning Gizmo's extension backend, to maximize immediate usefulness of existing Pi extensions.
Keep `AgentSession` in-process rather than switching Gizmo to Pi's RPC runtime; use `"rpc"` mode only for extension binding so `ctx.hasUI === true` and `ctx.mode === 'rpc'`.
Each `ctx.ui` call becomes a session-scoped WebSocket protocol event (`session.extensionUi.request` / `.respond`) with a unique UI request id.
Implement full-parity Svelte dialogs for select, confirm, input, and editor, including timeout countdowns, AbortSignal cancellation, Escape dismissal, keyboard navigation, and focus trapping.
Map notifications, statuses, widgets, editor text, working state, themes, and tool-expansion directly to Gizmo primitives rather than treating them as no-ops.

Handle TUI widgets in three tiers: text arrays render natively; simple Pi TUI components use a compatibility renderer to formatted/preformatted web content; interactive/custom TUI components fall back to unsupported with optional browser companions, rather than embedding a terminal emulator in the browser.

Add a separate `ExtensionUIStore` (not in `AgentStore`) with `$state` fields for dialogs, notifications, statuses, widgets, and working state, scoped by `{sessionId, extensionId, key}` to prevent collisions.

Attribute every UI request with `extensionPath` / `sourceInfo`, ideally by changing Pi to expose a scoped `uiContext.forExtension(...)`, so ownership, cleanup, trust display, and reload behavior are correct.

On session reload, switch, fork, disconnect, or deletion: cancel unresolved dialogs, clear statuses/widgets, abort pending UI promises, ignore late responses, dispose web components, and rebuild UI state.
Use Gizmo semantic design tokens for the web-native component SDK; do not let extensions depend directly on application CSS.
Provide an optional, parallel web-native `gizmo.ui.custom({component, props, presentation})` mechanism later; existing `ctx.ui.custom()` initially returns `undefined` matching current RPC behavior.

Recommended phased order: (1) attributed `ExtensionUIContext`, (2) bind in `"rpc"` mode, (3) protocol types, (4) confirm/select/input/editor, (5) notifications/statuses/text widgets, (6) editor text, paste, working, tool expansion, (7) themes, (8) `@gizmo/extension-ui` component library, (9) optional browser replacements for terminal-only `custom()`, (10) migrate individual Gizmo extensions onto Pi backends.
